title: Python slot claim: payload fully materialized by cbor2.loads before size/count checks (decode asymmetry with Rust)
description: Codereview finding (s61e security pass, reviewer kimi-k3), P3. python/src/lichen/gateway/slot_claim.py:263: cbor2.loads(payload) builds the entire slots list (~28B/int) before the MAX_SLOTS_PER_SUPERFRAME count check at :275 runs; Rust reads the CBOR array head and rejects count > 4096 before allocating (slot.rs:567-570). Attacker-chosen payload size drives memory/CPU before rejection. On the LoRa radio path this is bounded by the SCHC reassembly buffer, so in-threat-model exposure is modest — but the decode asymmetry is real and the fix is cheap: reject the envelope/payload above a byte cap before cbor2.loads (a max-size legit claim payload is ~21 KB: 4096 x 5-byte u32 + map overhead). Add a payload-length pre-check plus a test with a syntactically huge slots array.
close_reason: Resolved at HEAD without further change: the bead's requested byte-cap pre-check and test already landed via the merge of s61e-era work. slot_claim.py defines MAX_CLAIM_ENVELOPE_BYTES = 24_576 with a docstring that names this exact bead (prgb) and the exact rationale (max legit claim ~21.1 KB = 4096 x 5-byte u32 slots + map overhead + COSE wrapper; 24 KB bounds pre-rejection decode work because Python cannot read the CBOR head without decoding, unlike Rust slot.rs:567-570). decode_cose checks len(envelope) > MAX_CLAIM_ENVELOPE_BYTES before any cbor2.loads, and test_oversized_envelope_rejected_before_decode (test_slot_claim_cose_vectors.py) pins both the cap firing before decode and a real envelope fitting under it. Payload bytes are a subset of the envelope, so the envelope cap bounds payload materialization. Residual decode asymmetry (Rust head-count check vs Python byte cap) is the documented equivalent mitigation, not an open defect. Also re-verified this session: full python/tests/gateway suite green.
